payload.title: What Are the Palestinian Wedding Traditions You Did Not Know?
payload.excerpt: From the jaha and henna night to the zaffeh, dabke and tatreez: 12 Palestinian wedding traditions explained, and how to bring them to your wedding.
payload.author: Wedded Wonderland
key_takeaways: Palestinian wedding celebrations often run over several days, beginning with the tulbeh, the formal asking made by the groom's family.
UNESCO lists Palestinian embroidery (2021) and dabkeh (2023), and in 2024 added henna as an element shared by several countries.
Most embroidery motifs had names rather than fixed meanings, while colour and overall design signalled a woman's region and status.
Smartraveller advises Australians not to travel to Palestine, so couples bring these customs to a wedding at home or elsewhere, with space planned for the zaffeh, dabke and henna night.

faq.q: What happens at a Palestinian wedding?
faq.a: Celebrations often run over several days. They usually begin with the tulbeh, the formal asking at the bride's family home, and continue through a sahra evening, a henna gathering, the zaffeh procession, dabke and a shared meal.

faq.q: What do Palestinians wear to weddings?
faq.a: The bride may wear a hand-embroidered thobe, with the most ornate tatreez saved for the wedding; it may honour her hometown and include coins and jewellery. Colours and designs traditionally showed a woman's region and status. Families differ, so ask the couple what they have planned.

faq.q: What should guests wear to a Palestinian wedding?
faq.a: There is no single dress code across families, so take your cue from the invitation or ask the couple. Dress for a long evening on your feet: you may well be invited into a dabke line.

faq.q: What is the zaffeh at a Palestinian wedding?
faq.a: The zaffeh is the wedding procession; processionals (zeffat) are part of the Palestinian wedding singer's repertoire. Drums and a reed pipe are often told as its sound.

faq.q: How long does a Palestinian wedding last?
faq.a: Often several days, sometimes a week, though families in the diaspora have adapted the schedule. Many couples now hold the asking, a henna night and the wedding as separate events.

faq.q: What are Palestinian Christian wedding traditions?
faq.a: Palestinian Christian families marry in church, following their own church's rites. Our sources do not tie the henna night, dabke or tatreez to one faith, so ask the couple which customs their families keep.
